what: Coupang is South Korea's largest online retailer. It owns the inventory and the delivery network, which lets it guarantee next-morning or same-day delivery across the country, and it also runs food delivery, streaming and the luxury site Farfetch.
customers: South Korean households above all, plus Taiwanese customers and Farfetch buyers worldwide.
money: first-party retail sales and marketplace fees in Korea
Taiwan expansion, Eats food delivery, Play streaming and Farfetch
moat: A nationwide logistics network with its own drivers and warehouses, built at enormous cost, that no Korean competitor can match for delivery speed.
risks: It reported a loss as it invested in Taiwan and Farfetch
Net margin on the core business is about 1%
Taiwan expansion and Farfetch both consume cash
Korean regulators have scrutinised its marketplace practices
opportunities: Revenue grew about 14% last year and about 19% a year over three years
Analysts see large upside, with a median target well above the current price
The Korean core business is profitable and funds the expansion
watch: Product commerce margins and losses in the developing offerings segment.
